full_judgment:
"The crux of the writ petition involves that the then Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 3rd Court, Sylhet decreed the land in question in favour of the petitioner and declared that the land is not a vested property. It also appears from Annexure-C to the writ petition that Miscellaneous (A) Case No.12 of 1999 was dismissed for default. It further appears that in Order No.3 dated 5-6-2000 (Annexure-D-1 to the writ petitioner) it was observed that. 

 11. This Court sitting in writ jurisdiction is under a duty to examine the entire relevant evidence on record and if it refuses to consider important evidence having direct bearing on the disputed issue and the error, which arises, is of a magnitude that it gives birth to a substantial question of law and facts, the High Court is fully authorized to set aside the finding and on this score alone, we are of the view that this review petition is maintainable. The Supreme Court of Pakistan in the case of Mohd. Amir Khan vs Controller of Estate Duty, reported in PLD 1962 (SC) 335 = 14 DLR (SC) 276, had considered the scope and extent of the power of review under Article 161 of the Constitution of 1956 and Kaikaus, J made some observation therein: 

 14. It was brought to the notice of this Court that the then Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 3rd Court, Sylhet decreed the land in question in favour of the review opposite party (writ petitioner) and declared that the land is not a vested property. It was also brought to the notice of this Court that Miscellaneous WO Case No.12 of 1999 was dismissed for default.
